# Driver Compliance Hub

> Free, practical FMCSA guidance for U.S. owner-operators and small fleets. The site covers initial driver qualification file items, annual reviews, medical certification updates, Clearinghouse queries, and a browser-only printable checklist. Information is general guidance, not legal advice. Last reviewed: 2026-05-24.

## About this site

Driver Compliance Hub organizes official-source-based compliance information into plain-language pages and free tools. The checklist builder runs in the visitor's browser and does not store driver records, accept uploads, or require accounts.

Please attribute cited site content as "Driver Compliance Hub" and confirm regulatory requirements through the linked FMCSA source pages.

## Core pages

- [Home](/): Compliance topics, guided checklist builder, print action, and official FMCSA source links.
- [Employment Application](/checklist/employment-application): 49 CFR 391.21 application contents and retention context.
- [Initial Motor Vehicle Record (MVR)](/checklist/initial-mvr): 49 CFR 391.23 initial MVR inquiry and annual-review context.
- [Road Test & Certification](/checklist/road-test): 49 CFR 391.31 road test documentation and accepted equivalents.
- [Medical Examiner Certificate](/checklist/medical-certificate): Medical verification and current NRII transition exemption.
- [Verify Medical Examiner](/verify-examiner): Official National Registry link and safe access guidance.
- [Safety Performance History](/checklist/safety-performance-history): Investigation and driver rights context.

## Key facts shown on the site

- Motor carriers maintain driver qualification files under 49 CFR Part 391.
- At least once every 12 months, applicable carriers obtain and review an MVR and retain a dated review note.
- Employers of CDL drivers conduct pre-employment and annual Clearinghouse queries as required; the Clearinghouse keeps query history, while employers retain records of limited consent for 3 years.
- FMCSA's temporary NRII exemption is effective April 11 through October 11, 2026, allowing certain interstate CDL/CLP drivers and motor carriers to rely on a paper MEC for up to 60 days after issuance.

## Disclaimer

Content is for general information about U.S. federal regulations. It is not legal advice. Always consult current FMCSA materials and qualified counsel for compliance decisions.
